description: This comprehensive study guide covers the fundamental and advanced concepts of geometry, including lines, angles, triangles, circles, and polygons, along with their key properties and core formulas.

sections.title: Lines and Angles
sections.description: Fundamental properties of points, lines, and the geometric angles formed by their intersections.

key_concepts.explanation: An angle that measures greater than 0° and less than 90°.
An angle that measures greater than 90° and less than 180°.

results: The sum of the measures of both angles is exactly 90°.
The sum of the measures of both angles is exactly 180°.

sections.title: Triangles
sections.description: Properties, classification, and core mathematical formulas governing three-sided polygons.

key_concepts.explanation: A line segment connecting a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side.
The point of intersection where all three medians of a triangle meet. It divides each median in a strict 2:1 ratio from the vertex.

sections.title: Circles
sections.description: Properties of a planar shape consisting of all points equidistant from a fixed central point.

equations: Area of a Circle: π * r^2
Area of a Sector: (θ/360) * π * r^2

key_concepts.explanation: A straight line segment whose endpoints both lie on the circumference of the circle. The longest chord is the diameter.
A coplanar straight line that intersects a circle at exactly a single point without entering its interior.

results: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (forming a 90° angle).
The lengths of two tangent segments drawn from a shared external point to a circle are equal.

sections.title: Polygons
sections.description: Geometric properties and angular rules of closed, two-dimensional shapes bounded by three or more straight lines.

steps.title: Finding the Total Interior Sum
steps.detail: Calculate the total sum of all interior angles using the formula (n-2)*180°, substituting 'n' with the total number of polygon sides.

steps.title: Calculating a Single Interior Angle of a Regular Polygon
steps.detail: Divide the total calculated sum of the interior angles by the total number of sides 'n' to find the value of each individual interior angle.
